chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'And pilgrimage to the House is incumbent upon men for the sake of Allah, (upon) every one who is able to undertake the journey to it.' What does He mean by this?
He (peace be upon him) replied, 'He means that whoever has a healthy body, a route free from trouble, proper provision, and a mode of transportation.'

key_terms.مُخْلَىٰ سَبِيلَهُ: His route is clear/free from trouble

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions of 'ability' (istita'ah) required for the obligation of Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the condition of *istita'ah* (capability) for Hajj by specifying four tangible prerequisites: physical health, a secure route, adequate provisions, and transport. This definition aligns with the Shia juristic consensus that obligation is lifted if any of these specific material or physical conditions are absent, emphasizing that divine command is never beyond one's capacity.
